_comment: A3 PRIORITY PROPAGATION (operating-layer Phase C). The cycle's priority, written where scripts/ops/render_session_brief.py renders it into CLAUDE.md -- the only surface that reaches a session before its first tool call. THE CHANNEL ALREADY WORKED; nothing wrote a priority for it to carry, so a decision taken with the operator reached the next session only if a human retyped it. That is the gap this file closes, and the whole of it. ⚠️ IT DOES NOT MAKE ANYONE FOLLOW THE PRIORITY -- it removes the excuse of not knowing it. Do not describe it as enforcement. ⚠️ `current` may be null: NO PRIORITY SET and RENDERER BROKEN must never render identically, so the renderer prints an explicit line for null rather than falling silent. Editing this file changes CLAUDE.md's generated brief -- re-render with `python3 scripts/ops/render_session_brief.py --write`, never by hand-editing the block.

current.priority: Keep implementing the operating-model plan — and SPECIFICALLY build the infrastructure that lets a MANAGER session actually manage the sessions it spawns. Operator-directed 2026-09-02T21:50Z, after a day in which the manager lost track of its own sub-sessions twice.
current.why: MEASURED 2026-09-02, not asserted. (1) All 15 sub-sessions the day manager spawned read state='working' in SESSIONS.json while list_sessions reported 14 IDLE and 1 RUNNING, one idle for 8 hours -- session_registry.py exposes exactly four verbs (status, reconcile, register, confirm), ZERO of which write a terminal state, and cmd_reconcile only PRINTs. (2) A sub-session opened PR #10859 at 20:56Z and its own manager did not learn of it until 21:12Z, found only by polling the author's session summary after a scheduled sweep prompted it. Nothing surfaced it. (3) The manager undrafted and armed #10857 while its author was still RUNNING, because there was no way to ask -- and nothing objected. ⚠️ THE GAP IS THE MISSING READ, NOT A MISSING CHANNEL: a RUNNING session cannot be reached, an IDLE one CAN be woken, and nothing tells the manager which it is.
current.what_it_means_for_a_session: If you are the manager: the highest-value thing you can build is the ability to SEE and REACH your own sub-sessions -- a close-time writer plus a reaper (a session that dies cannot close itself), or state DERIVED at read time from a live observation so it cannot go stale. ⚠️ CLOUD ROUTINES ARE AN ALLOWED TOOL FOR THIS AND ARE PROBABLY PART OF THE ANSWER -- see routine_scope_correction below before reasoning about them. The general operating-model build continues underneath this; manager-control is the named priority within it, not a replacement for it.
current.routine_scope_correction: ⚠️ 'NO CLOUD ROUTINE' IS NOT A GENERAL RULE AND MUST NOT BE WRITTEN AS ONE. Operator, 2026-09-02T21:50Z, correcting the day manager verbatim: "when I said no cloud routines that wasn't 'don't use that tool', it was don't use that as a Band-Aid for something that needs to be an actual routine. You CAN spawn off cloud routines, especially if that's gonna give you better control over the session. That was for that specific thing, not a general rule. I don't want it written into the rules as a general rule." WHAT WAS ACTUALLY REFUSED: using a session-bound Routine as a substitute for durable infrastructure -- the specific case was the hourly work digest, where the right answer is the VM systemd timer in #10859 because a session-bound Routine dies with its session. WHAT IS ALLOWED: Routines as a real mechanism, and explicitly for MANAGER CONTROL over sub-sessions, which is this cycle's priority. ⚠️ THE ERROR THAT PRODUCED THIS ROW IS ITS OWN FINDING: the day manager took a scoped operator statement and hardened it into a standing prohibition, writing 'NO CLAUDE ROUTINE, in any form' into a spawn prompt, a checklist row, a work object and a merged PR body. That is the SAME over-generalisation class it had already caught itself in twice the same day (the sub-session 403, measured both ways; and 'no supervise verb', true only of RUNNING sessions). Three instances in one day.
current.operator_sequencing_2026_09_03: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE, 2026-09-03, verbatim: "I want us to first finish building the new workflow, then we'll review and update the whole roadmap together, then we can get started on actual work." THREE PHASES, IN ORDER, and the ordering is the instruction. (1) FINISH THE WORKFLOW BUILD -- the operating-layer phases and the manager-control capability. (2) REVIEW AND UPDATE THE ROADMAP *TOGETHER WITH THE OPERATOR* -- this is a JOINT act, not something a session does alone and presents; a session that rewrites the roadmap unilaterally has skipped the phase, not completed it. (3) ONLY THEN start substantive trading/research work. ⚠️ WHAT THIS RULES OUT: spawning trading, strategy, ML or research work while phase (1) is unfinished -- including under a spawn-priority exception, and including work that is individually well-justified. The exception mechanism grants a displacement of the CYCLE PRIORITY; it does not grant a displacement of this SEQUENCING. Those are different controls and an approved exception must not be read as covering both. ⚠️ IT DOES NOT RULE OUT: keeping the live system safe. An operational incident, a money-at-risk defect, or work whose DELAY causes irreversible loss is not 'actual work' in this sense and is never gated behind a build phase.

history.priority: Stand up the operating layer's STEERING half. The system built EXECUTION and INTEGRITY to a high standard and never built the steering: of 24 declared functions, 5 work, 14 are partial and 5 are missing outright, and all five missing ones are steering.
history.why: Measured 2026-09-01 across the working tree, populations stated in the design series: backlog net +425 rows in August against +37 in May; 196 dated sprint logs of which 1.0% deployed to real money; 256 of 370 research units superseded before anyone read them; 1 of 117 dispositions producing an action; 21 of 32 milestones simultaneously active. The root cause is not rigour or effort -- both are strong -- it is that nothing removes anything.
history.what_it_means_for_a_session: Prefer work that makes the system steer over work that makes it execute better. If you are about to start something that is neither the current phase nor pulled by a held-up stage, that is the thing to re-argue before starting it.
history.basis_note: DECIDED, not MEASURED. The operator directed the operating-model redesign on 2026-09-01; the measurements above are the evidence that informed it, not the derivation of it. E1 constraint diagnosis does not exist yet, so this priority is operator-set rather than computed -- which is a legitimate source (A2 priority is operator-set by design) but a DIFFERENT one, and recording it as a constraint finding would be the unprovenanced conclusion this repo keeps paying for.
history.review_cadence_note: Weekly, matching the intent's review_cadence. Past review_by the renderer marks it STALE rather than dropping it: a priority nobody re-affirmed is still the last thing decided, and hiding it would be worse than showing it with its age.
